extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of Italian medieval political and constitutional history
extracted.subtask_description: A historical and constitutional account of medieval Tuscan and Emilian republics (Siena, Bologna, Florence), describing forms of government, electoral procedures, magistracies, councils, and the civic effects of different constitutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid concentration of sovereignty in a single assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: No matter whether the assembly consists of many or few, nobles or commons, great or little, rich or poor, substantial men or the rabble, the effects are the same: no order, no safety, no liberty because no government of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text argues that sovereignty vested in one assembly (legislative, executive, and judicial authority concentrated) leads to perpetual divisions, seditions, and civil wars. To produce order and liberty, powers must be separated and factions legally separated from each other and empowered to control each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred form of government: produces love of law and commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a form of government which produces a love of law, liberty, and country, instead of disorder, irregularity, and faction; it produces independence of spirit, undaunted bravery, esteem of merit over wealth, simplicity, sincerity, generosity, desire of knowledge, security of property, and opportunities for commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author contrasts factional republics (which cultivate factional loyalty, hatred, and continual war) with a constitution that channels energies into law and commerce; such a government better fosters civic virtues and material prosperity. This functions as a normative criterion for evaluating constitutions: prefer those that secure law, property, and commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional design: popular control of purse and legislative inquests plus a single executive
rubrics_metrics.description: A constitution in which the people reserve to themselves the absolute control of their purses, one essential branch of the legislature, and the inquest of grievances and state crimes, will produce patriotism, bravery, simplicity, and science; and that infinitely better for the order, security, and tranquillity they will enjoy, by putting the executive power into one hand, which it becomes their interest, as well as that of the nobles, to watch and control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text recommends a specific package: (1) people's control of finances, (2) an essential legislative branch retained by the people, and (3) investigatory powers over grievances and state crimes, combined with a unitary executive. This configuration is presented as instrumental to producing civic virtue and mutual checks (the people and nobles have aligned incentives to oversee a single executive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed lottery-and-choice electoral procedures to prevent faction and corruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Elections combine lot with choice and rotation: tribes draw lots and elect small elector groups (e.g., ten electors per tribe, then forty electors, then 600), exclusion of certain classes (e.g., mean and poor artisans), age limits (no minors under 18), restrictions on relatives (cannot be electors within third degree), payment into the treasury as qualification, and prohibitions on openly seeking office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed procedural devices (urns with blank and written tickets, children drawing, multiple stages of selection, prohibitions on relations and on candidates who solicit office, financial payment requirement, age and residence restrictions) are described as safeguards against ambition, faction, and bribery. Secret selection of electors and confinement during selection (e.g., locking up electors overnight) are recommended to limit external corruption; deadlocks revert to wider suffrage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberative and voting procedures for councils and magistrates
rubrics_metrics.description: Councils follow set procedures: business must be posted in chancery before convocation; chancellor proposes the subject publicly; orators speak; votes may be taken secretly by notary or openly (audible votes), by white and black beans, or by physical division of the assembly; decisions are recorded, published, and decrees cannot be superseded until recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text provides multiple modalities for deliberation and vote-counting (secret written opinions, public audible votes, token methods, spatial division), with notaries recording speeches and decrees. These procedural norms are presented as institutional practices that underpin legitimacy, record-keeping, and orderly governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magistracy organization and anti-nepotism / term limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Magistrates (ordinary and extraordinary) are chosen annually; ordinary magistrates administer routine functions while extraordinary are appointed for special business; one year gap required before re-accepting office; specific qualifications (age minimum ~36, reputation, property/residence requirements) and oaths of integrity are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual rotation, ineligibility for immediate reappointment, age and reputation thresholds, and mandated oaths are described as legal safeguards to limit ambition, ensure experience and probity, and maintain accountability in public office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-corruption measures during sensitive elections
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain elections (e.g., pretor), forty electors are secluded (locked up) with selected merchants and bankers to prevent corruption; if they cannot agree by a high threshold (e.g., 27 of 40), authority of election is lost and broader councils are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seclusion of electors, inclusion of respected economic actors, and high consensus thresholds are cited as measures to reduce external influence and ensure a credible selection. The fallback to wider suffrage if deadlock occurs is a practical resolution to impasses.
